## Each round of k-means makes the groups tighter {#clustering .idea data-page="Clustering with k-means" data-href="../chapters/08-unsupervised-learning/clustering.html"}

```{=html}
<div class="visual">
<svg viewBox="0 0 1200 420" role="img" aria-label="k-means in three steps. Place the centres at random. Assign each point to its nearest centre. Move each centre to the average of its points. The last two steps repeat until no point changes group.">
  <g>
    <rect class="card" x="0" y="0" width="380" height="350" rx="14"/>
    <text class="lab f-accent" x="28" y="46">1 PLACE CENTRES</text>
    <g transform="translate(40 80)" class="f-grey"><circle cx="40" cy="60" r="9"/><circle cx="70" cy="40" r="9"/><circle cx="60" cy="90" r="9"/><circle cx="100" cy="70" r="9"/><circle cx="210" cy="150" r="9"/><circle cx="240" cy="130" r="9"/><circle cx="250" cy="180" r="9"/><circle cx="280" cy="160" r="9"/><circle cx="220" cy="190" r="9"/><circle cx="50" cy="200" r="9"/><circle cx="80" cy="220" r="9"/><circle cx="110" cy="190" r="9"/></g>
    <g transform="translate(40 80)"><path class="f-blue s-fg" stroke-width="2" d="M160,40 l10,18 l-20,0 z"/><path class="f-orange s-fg" stroke-width="2" d="M150,170 l10,18 l-20,0 z"/></g>
    <text class="sm" x="28" y="330">At random</text>
  </g>
  <line class="wire arrow" x1="388" y1="175" x2="432" y2="175"/>
  <g transform="translate(440 0)">
    <rect class="card" x="0" y="0" width="360" height="350" rx="14"/>
    <text class="lab f-accent" x="28" y="46">2 ASSIGN</text>
    <g transform="translate(30 80)">
      <g class="f-blue"><circle cx="40" cy="60" r="9"/><circle cx="70" cy="40" r="9"/><circle cx="60" cy="90" r="9"/><circle cx="100" cy="70" r="9"/><circle cx="240" cy="130" r="9"/></g>
      <g class="f-orange"><circle cx="210" cy="150" r="9"/><circle cx="250" cy="180" r="9"/><circle cx="280" cy="160" r="9"/><circle cx="220" cy="190" r="9"/><circle cx="50" cy="200" r="9"/><circle cx="80" cy="220" r="9"/><circle cx="110" cy="190" r="9"/></g>
      <path class="f-blue s-fg" stroke-width="2" d="M160,40 l10,18 l-20,0 z"/><path class="f-orange s-fg" stroke-width="2" d="M150,170 l10,18 l-20,0 z"/>
    </g>
    <text class="sm" x="28" y="330">Each to its nearest centre</text>
  </g>
  <line class="wire arrow" x1="808" y1="175" x2="852" y2="175"/>
  <g transform="translate(860 0)">
    <rect class="card" x="0" y="0" width="340" height="350" rx="14"/>
    <text class="lab f-accent" x="28" y="46">3 MOVE CENTRES</text>
    <g transform="translate(20 80)">
      <g class="f-blue"><circle cx="40" cy="60" r="9"/><circle cx="70" cy="40" r="9"/><circle cx="60" cy="90" r="9"/><circle cx="100" cy="70" r="9"/><circle cx="240" cy="130" r="9"/></g>
      <g class="f-orange"><circle cx="210" cy="150" r="9"/><circle cx="250" cy="180" r="9"/><circle cx="280" cy="160" r="9"/><circle cx="220" cy="190" r="9"/><circle cx="50" cy="200" r="9"/><circle cx="80" cy="220" r="9"/><circle cx="110" cy="190" r="9"/></g>
      <path class="f-blue s-fg" stroke-width="2" d="M102,60 l10,18 l-20,0 z"/><path class="f-orange s-fg" stroke-width="2" d="M172,178 l10,18 l-20,0 z"/>
    </g>
    <text class="sm" x="28" y="330">To the average of its points</text>
  </g>
  <path class="wire arrow" d="M1030,360 C1030,410 620,410 620,362"/>
  <text class="sm mute" x="660" y="412">repeat until nothing changes</text>
</svg>
</div>
```

::: {.takeaway}
Where k-means ends depends on where it starts, so run it from many starts and keep the best.
:::

::: notes
Clustering sorts rows into groups of similar rows, with no labels to learn from. k-means places k centres, assigns every station to its nearest centre, and moves each centre to the average of its stations. Each round makes the groups tighter, measured by the within-cluster sum of squares. The answer depends on the random start, so it is run from many starts and the tightest result is kept. Counts are logged and standardised first, in a recipe.
:::

## Two clusters recover the hard and soft seabed {.example}

::: {.plot}
::: {.card}
![](figures/08-unsupervised-learning/clustering/fig-clusters-1.png){fig-alt="Each station's depth, split into the soft-bottom cluster and the hard-bottom cluster, coloured by the seabed the survey recorded. Almost every station in each cluster has the matching seabed, and each cluster spans most of the depth range."}
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
From 24 species counts alone, only 15 stations ended up out of place. Depth played no part.
:::

::: notes
The community matrix counts 24 taxa at each station. k-means with two clusters, given only those counts, split the stations into hard and soft seabed with 15 out of place, although the seabed was never given to it. It did not split by depth. Depth changes the species gradually, with no gap to split on. k-means will return groups from any table, so this agreement is the evidence, not the clusters themselves.
:::

## Shuffling each column removes the groups {#choosing-the-number-of-clusters .idea data-page="Choosing the number of clusters" data-href="../chapters/08-unsupervised-learning/choosing-the-number-of-clusters.html"}

```{=html}
<div class="visual">
<svg viewBox="0 0 1200 420" role="img" aria-label="Two tables. In the observed table the rows fall into two groups, so values of the same colour line up across the columns. In the shuffled table each column has been shuffled on its own, so every column keeps its values but the rows no longer form groups.">
  <rect class="card" x="0" y="0" width="500" height="410" rx="14"/>
  <text class="head" x="32" y="56">Observed</text>
  <g transform="translate(60 90)">
    <g class="f-blue"><rect x="0" y="0" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="95" y="0" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="190" y="0" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="285" y="0" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="0" y="50" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="95" y="50" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="190" y="50" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="285" y="50" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="0" y="100" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="95" y="100" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="190" y="100" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="285" y="100" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/></g>
    <g class="f-orange"><rect x="0" y="150" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="95" y="150" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="190" y="150" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="285" y="150" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="0" y="200" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="95" y="200" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="190" y="200" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect x="285" y="200" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/></g>
  </g>
  <text class="sm" x="32" y="380">Rows fall into groups</text>
  <line class="wire arrow thick" x1="520" y1="200" x2="600" y2="200"/>
  <text class="sm mid" x="560" y="250">shuffle</text><text class="sm mid" x="560" y="280">each column</text>
  <rect class="card" x="620" y="0" width="580" height="410" rx="14"/>
  <text class="head" x="652" y="56">Shuffled</text>
  <g transform="translate(680 90)">
    <rect class="f-blue" x="0" y="0" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-orange" x="95" y="0" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-blue" x="190" y="0" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-blue" x="285" y="0" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/>
    <rect class="f-orange" x="0" y="50" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-blue" x="95" y="50" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-blue" x="190" y="50" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-orange" x="285" y="50" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/>
    <rect class="f-blue" x="0" y="100" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-blue" x="95" y="100" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-orange" x="190" y="100" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-blue" x="285" y="100" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/>
    <rect class="f-blue" x="0" y="150" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-orange" x="95" y="150" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-blue" x="190" y="150" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-blue" x="285" y="150" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/>
    <rect class="f-orange" x="0" y="200" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-blue" x="95" y="200" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-orange" x="190" y="200" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/><rect class="f-orange" x="285" y="200" width="80" height="40" rx="5"/>
  </g>
  <text class="sm" x="652" y="380">Same values, no groups, a baseline</text>
</svg>
</div>
```

::: {.takeaway}
The number of groups is a choice. A shuffled baseline shows which number stands out.
:::

::: notes
k-means needs the number of clusters as an input, so it is a choice that needs evidence. The within-cluster sum of squares always falls as k rises, and its elbow often has no clear bend. The silhouette width compares each station's distance to its own cluster with its distance to the nearest other. Both measures need a baseline. Shuffling each column on its own keeps every column's values and removes any groups, so clustering the shuffled table shows what these values give with no structure at all.
:::

## Two clusters stand furthest above the shuffled baseline {.example}

::: {.plot}
::: {.card}
![](figures/08-unsupervised-learning/choosing-the-number-of-clusters/fig-k-sweep-1.png){fig-alt="Left, the within-cluster sum of squares for two to eight clusters, falling steadily for both the observed and shuffled data. Right, the average silhouette width, highest for the observed data at two clusters and well above the shuffled band there."}
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
At two clusters the silhouette was 3.5 times the shuffled value. Those are the hard and soft seabed.
:::

::: notes
The sum of squares falls steadily for the observed and the shuffled data alike, with no bend to choose by. The silhouette is highest at two clusters and stands furthest above the shuffled band there, three and a half times the shuffled value. A useful number of groups is not a true one, but here two clusters match a real division of the seabed.
:::

## A dendrogram nests groups within groups {#hierarchical-clustering .idea data-page="Hierarchical clustering" data-href="../chapters/08-unsupervised-learning/hierarchical-clustering.html"}

```{=html}
<div class="visual">
<svg viewBox="0 0 1200 420" role="img" aria-label="A dendrogram over eight stations, built by joining the two closest groups again and again. A dashed line cutting across it gives three groups. Beside it, four linkage rules measure the distance between two groups by the nearest members, the furthest members, all pairs on average, or Ward's increase in spread.">
  <g transform="translate(40 20)">
    <g class="none s-fg" stroke-width="4">
      <path d="M20,330 V270 H80 V330"/><path d="M140,330 V290 H200 V330"/><path d="M50,270 V200 H170 V290"/>
      <path d="M260,330 V280 H320 V330"/><path d="M380,330 V250 H290 V280"/>
      <path d="M440,330 V300 H500 V330"/><path d="M335,250 V160 H470 V300"/>
      <path d="M110,200 V80 H402 V160"/>
    </g>
    <g class="f-blue"><circle cx="20" cy="340" r="12"/><circle cx="80" cy="340" r="12"/><circle cx="140" cy="340" r="12"/><circle cx="200" cy="340" r="12"/></g>
    <g class="f-orange"><circle cx="260" cy="340" r="12"/><circle cx="320" cy="340" r="12"/><circle cx="380" cy="340" r="12"/></g>
    <g class="f-green"><circle cx="440" cy="340" r="12"/><circle cx="500" cy="340" r="12"/></g>
    <line class="none s-red dash" stroke-width="4" x1="-20" y1="220" x2="540" y2="220"/>
    <text class="sm f-red" x="550" y="228" font-weight="700">cut</text>
    <text class="sm mute" x="0" y="390">Cut lower for more groups, higher for fewer</text>
  </g>
  <rect class="card" x="700" y="0" width="500" height="410" rx="14"/>
  <text class="lab mute" x="730" y="46">LINKAGE, THE DISTANCE BETWEEN GROUPS</text>
  <g>
    <text class="head" x="730" y="110">Single</text><text class="sm mute" x="930" y="110">nearest members</text>
    <text class="head" x="730" y="190">Complete</text><text class="sm mute" x="930" y="190">furthest members</text>
    <text class="head" x="730" y="270">Average</text><text class="sm mute" x="930" y="270">all pairs</text>
    <text class="head" x="730" y="350">Ward</text><text class="sm mute" x="930" y="350">growth in spread</text>
  </g>
</svg>
</div>
```

::: {.takeaway}
One tree holds every number of groups, but it never undoes a join.
:::

::: notes
Hierarchical clustering starts with every station on its own and joins the two closest groups again and again. The joins form a tree, a dendrogram, and cutting it at a height gives any number of groups, which nest inside each other. How close two groups are is set by the linkage rule. Single linkage uses their nearest members, complete their furthest, average all pairs, and Ward's rule the growth in spread, the same measure k-means uses.
:::

## Linkage decides whether the tree chains or finds the seabed {.example}

::: {.plot}
::: {.card}
![](figures/08-unsupervised-learning/hierarchical-clustering/fig-linkage-1.png){fig-alt="Left, agreement with the recorded seabed for trees cut into two to six groups under four linkage rules. Ward is highest at two groups and single linkage is near zero throughout. Right, the share of stations in the largest group, near 1 for single and average linkage."}
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Agreement with the seabed ran from 0.005 for single linkage to 0.89 for Ward.
:::

::: notes
The same stations and distances give very different trees under different linkage rules. Agreement with the recorded seabed is measured by the adjusted Rand index, 1 for identical groupings and 0 for chance. Single and average linkage chain, leaving nearly every station in one group, which is the sign to look for. Ward's linkage found the seabed, and its two groups matched k-means' with an index of 0.94.
:::

## Each component is the direction of most remaining spread {#principal-component-analysis .idea data-page="Principal component analysis" data-href="../chapters/08-unsupervised-learning/principal-component-analysis.html"}

```{=html}
<div class="visual">
<svg viewBox="0 0 1200 420" role="img" aria-label="A tilted oval cloud of points. The first principal component runs along its longest direction and the second at right angles to it. A point's position along the new axes is its score. The weights that build each component from the columns are its loadings.">
  <g transform="translate(330 210) rotate(-28)">
    <ellipse class="t-blue" cx="0" cy="0" rx="270" ry="110" opacity="0.7"/>
    <g class="f-blue"><circle cx="-220" cy="20" r="8"/><circle cx="-180" cy="-30" r="8"/><circle cx="-150" cy="40" r="8"/><circle cx="-110" cy="-10" r="8"/><circle cx="-80" cy="60" r="8"/><circle cx="-60" cy="-50" r="8"/><circle cx="-20" cy="20" r="8"/><circle cx="10" cy="-30" r="8"/><circle cx="40" cy="50" r="8"/><circle cx="70" cy="-10" r="8"/><circle cx="110" cy="40" r="8"/><circle cx="140" cy="-40" r="8"/><circle cx="170" cy="20" r="8"/><circle cx="210" cy="-20" r="8"/><circle cx="240" cy="10" r="8"/></g>
    <line class="none s-red arrow" stroke-width="6" x1="-280" y1="0" x2="300" y2="0" style="marker-end: url(#deck-arrow)"/>
    <line class="none s-orange" stroke-width="6" x1="0" y1="130" x2="0" y2="-130"/>
    <path class="f-orange" d="M0,-150 l12,22 l-24,0 z"/>
    <line class="none s-fg dash" stroke-width="2" x1="140" y1="-40" x2="140" y2="0"/>
  </g>
  <text class="head f-red" x="600" y="70">PC1</text>
  <text class="head f-orange" x="240" y="60">PC2</text>
  <rect class="card" x="720" y="40" width="480" height="340" rx="14"/>
  <text class="head" x="750" y="100">Loadings</text><text class="sm mute" x="750" y="136">weights that build a component</text><text class="sm mute" x="750" y="166">from the columns</text>
  <text class="head" x="750" y="236">Scores</text><text class="sm mute" x="750" y="272">a station's position</text><text class="sm mute" x="750" y="302">on each component</text>
</svg>
</div>
```

::: {.takeaway}
The first two components make a map of the stations, an ordination.
:::

::: notes
Principal component analysis builds new axes from the columns. The first runs along the direction of most spread, the second along the most remaining spread at right angles to it, and so on. Loadings are the weights that build a component from the columns, and a station's position on it is its score. Scale the columns first. The sign of a component is arbitrary, and R and scikit-learn gave opposite signs here.
:::

## Depth and seabed run diagonally across the map {.example}

::: {.plot}
::: {.card}
![](figures/08-unsupervised-learning/principal-component-analysis/fig-ordination-1.png){fig-alt="The 800 stations on the first two components, coloured by depth and shaped by seabed. Hard and soft bottom form two arms, and depth changes smoothly along them. Arrows for depth and hard bottom point diagonally, not along either axis."}
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
The first two components hold 29% of the variance. A component is not a gradient.
:::

::: notes
The first two components of the 24 taxon counts hold under a third of the variance, which is usual for species counts and does not mean the map shows nothing. The seabed shows as a boundary between two arms and depth as a smooth gradient. Both run at about 39 degrees to the nearest axis, because the two components hold nearly equal variance. PCA finds the plane, not the drivers within it.
:::

## A set share of the variance keeps noise as well {#dimensionality-reduction .idea data-page="How many components to keep" data-href="../chapters/08-unsupervised-learning/dimensionality-reduction.html"}

```{=html}
<div class="visual">
<svg viewBox="0 0 1200 420" role="img" aria-label="Three rules for how many of 24 components to keep. Keep 80 percent of the variance, which kept 16 and keeps noise too. Parallel analysis, keeping components above a shuffled baseline, which kept 3. Cross-validation of the model that uses the components, which kept 2 for predicting depth.">
  <g>
    <rect class="card" x="0" y="0" width="380" height="410" rx="14"/>
    <text class="head" x="28" y="56">80% of the variance</text>
    <text class="big f-red" x="28" y="190">16</text><text class="sm mute" x="100" y="190">of 24 kept</text>
    <text class="sm" x="28" y="320">Keeps noise</text><text class="sm" x="28" y="352">as well as structure</text>
  </g>
  <g transform="translate(410 0)">
    <rect class="card" x="0" y="0" width="380" height="410" rx="14"/>
    <text class="head" x="28" y="56">Shuffled baseline</text>
    <text class="big f-green" x="28" y="190">3</text><text class="sm mute" x="70" y="190">kept</text>
    <text class="sm" x="28" y="320">Keeps what holds</text><text class="sm" x="28" y="352">structure</text>
  </g>
  <g transform="translate(820 0)">
    <rect class="card" x="0" y="0" width="380" height="410" rx="14"/>
    <text class="head" x="28" y="56">Cross-validation</text>
    <text class="big f-blue" x="28" y="190">2</text><text class="sm mute" x="70" y="190">kept for depth</text>
    <text class="sm" x="28" y="320">Keeps what a model</text><text class="sm" x="28" y="352">needs to predict</text>
  </g>
</svg>
</div>
```

::: {.takeaway}
Structure and prediction each have their own test, and they can keep different numbers.
:::

::: notes
Components can replace the original columns as inputs to a model. A common rule keeps components until they hold 80 percent of the variance, but that keeps noise as well as structure. Parallel analysis keeps the components that hold more variance than they would in a shuffled table. When the components feed a model, cross-validate the model at each number of components, with the PCA inside the recipe. The two tests answer different questions. The third component held structure, rock against gravel, that predicting depth did not need.
:::

## Parallel analysis keeps far fewer components {.example}

::: {.plot}
::: {.card}
![](figures/08-unsupervised-learning/dimensionality-reduction/fig-baseline-1.png){fig-alt="The share of the variance held by each of 24 components, falling steeply over the first three and then slowly. A dashed line from shuffled data crosses the curve after the third component. A dotted line at component 16 marks where 80 percent of the variance is reached."}
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Three components stand above the shuffled line. The 80% rule would keep sixteen.
:::

::: notes
Each point is one component's share of the variance. The dashed line is the share the same component reaches in shuffled copies of the table. Only the first three stand above it, so only they hold structure. The 80 percent rule would keep going to the sixteenth component, mostly noise.
:::

## UMAP draws neighbourhoods, not distances {.example}

::: {.plot}
::: {.card}
![](figures/08-unsupervised-learning/dimensionality-reduction/fig-umap-1.png){fig-alt="UMAP maps of the community data and of a shuffled copy. The observed map shows two separate shapes that follow the seabed, with depth changing smoothly within them. The shuffled map is one featureless blob."}
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Read only its neighbourhoods. Run a shuffled copy through the same steps.
:::

::: notes
UMAP is a map made for looking at the stations. It keeps each station's neighbours close and bends everything else to fit, so the distances between groups and their sizes mean little. Neither depth nor seabed was given to it, yet the observed map separates the seabed and shows depth as a smooth change. The shuffled copy, made with the same settings, is one featureless blob, which is the check that the pattern is real.
:::

## Three checks stand in for held-out answers {#interpreting-patterns .idea data-page="Checking a pattern before reporting it" data-href="../chapters/08-unsupervised-learning/interpreting-patterns.html"}

```{=html}
<div class="visual">
<svg viewBox="0 0 1200 420" role="img" aria-label="Three checks before reporting a pattern. Does it come back when refitted on bootstrap samples? Is it a group, with a gap at the boundary, or a cut through a gradient? Does it match a recorded variable the method never saw?">
  <g>
    <rect class="card" x="0" y="0" width="380" height="410" rx="14"/>
    <circle class="f-accent" cx="48" cy="52" r="24"/><text class="mid f-bg" x="48" y="61" font-weight="700">1</text>
    <text class="head" x="28" y="130">Comes back</text>
    <g transform="translate(40 170)" class="f-blue"><rect x="0" y="0" width="60" height="40" rx="6"/><rect x="80" y="0" width="60" height="40" rx="6"/><rect x="160" y="0" width="60" height="40" rx="6"/><rect x="240" y="0" width="60" height="40" rx="6" class="f-orange"/></g>
    <text class="sm" x="28" y="320">Refit on bootstrap</text><text class="sm" x="28" y="352">samples of whole sites</text>
  </g>
  <g transform="translate(410 0)">
    <rect class="card" x="0" y="0" width="380" height="410" rx="14"/>
    <circle class="f-accent" cx="48" cy="52" r="24"/><text class="mid f-bg" x="48" y="61" font-weight="700">2</text>
    <text class="head" x="28" y="130">A gap, not a gradient</text>
    <g transform="translate(40 160)">
      <line class="axis" x1="0" y1="80" x2="300" y2="80"/>
      <rect class="f-blue" x="10" y="30" width="20" height="50"/><rect class="f-blue" x="34" y="10" width="20" height="70"/><rect class="f-blue" x="58" y="34" width="20" height="46"/>
      <rect class="f-blue" x="210" y="20" width="20" height="60"/><rect class="f-blue" x="234" y="0" width="20" height="80"/><rect class="f-blue" x="258" y="30" width="20" height="50"/>
      <line class="none s-red dash" stroke-width="3" x1="145" y1="-10" x2="145" y2="90"/>
    </g>
    <text class="sm" x="28" y="320">Real groups leave</text><text class="sm" x="28" y="352">few stations between</text>
  </g>
  <g transform="translate(820 0)">
    <rect class="card" x="0" y="0" width="380" height="410" rx="14"/>
    <circle class="f-accent" cx="48" cy="52" r="24"/><text class="mid f-bg" x="48" y="61" font-weight="700">3</text>
    <text class="head" x="28" y="130">Matches a record</text>
    <g transform="translate(40 170)"><rect class="t-blue s-blue" stroke-width="2" x="0" y="0" width="120" height="44" rx="22"/><text class="sm mid" x="60" y="30">cluster</text><text class="head mid" x="150" y="32">=</text><rect class="t-orange s-orange" stroke-width="2" x="180" y="0" width="120" height="44" rx="22"/><text class="sm mid" x="240" y="30">seabed</text></g>
    <text class="sm" x="28" y="320">A variable the method</text><text class="sm" x="28" y="352">never saw</text>

</div>
```

::: {.takeaway}
An unsupervised result has no answers to test against. These checks stand in for them.
:::

::: notes
A cluster has no held-out answers to be scored on, so three checks stand in. Refit on bootstrap samples, drawing whole sites, and see whether the same grouping comes back. Look at where stations sit between the two cluster centres, because real groups leave a gap and a gradient does not. And compare the grouping with a recorded variable the method never saw. In 60 bootstrap samples, 52 gave the seabed split and 8 a depth split.
:::

## A group leaves a gap where a gradient does not {.example}

::: {.plot}
::: {.card}
![](figures/08-unsupervised-learning/interpreting-patterns/fig-positions-1.png){fig-alt="Where each station sits between two cluster centres. For all stations, the seabed split leaves a gap at the boundary between two humps. For the soft bottom only, the split cuts through the middle of one broad spread."}
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
The soft-bottom split came back every time, yet it only cuts one broad gradient.
:::

::: notes
For all stations, the two clusters leave a clear gap at the boundary, the mark of real groups, and they match the recorded seabed. Clustering only the soft-bottom stations also gives a split that comes back in every bootstrap sample, but it cuts through the middle of one broad spread. Coming back is not enough. A split through a steady gradient falls in the same place every time. A checked pattern is still a hypothesis.
:::

## Key points {.closing}

::: {.closing}
::: {.points}
- k-means and hierarchical clustering return groups from any table.
- Compare cluster measures with a shuffled baseline to choose the number of groups.
- PCA makes a map of the stations. A component is not a driver.
- Keep components by a test of structure or of prediction, not a set share.
- Check that a pattern comes back, leaves a gap and matches a record.
:::

::: {.more}
The full section, with code in R and Python, is on the [course site](../chapters/08-unsupervised-learning/index.html).
:::
